\makepapertitle
\begin{paperabstract}
We ask what the best layout is under a fixed cost function, and how sure
we can be. We compare eight optimizers (hill climbing, SA, breakout
local search, tabu, GA, memetic, MAP-Elites, NSGA-II) under equal
budgets on a quadratic assignment problem with sparse trigram terms,
give a Gilmore–Lawler lower bound with dual ascent (90.3 \% gap at 30
free keys, 1.7 \% on the bigram part at 10 free keys), and certify
solutions window by window with exact search {[}TODO{]}. We report the
best layouts found for {[}TODO: ANSI-30, Corne-36, with layers{]} with
their per-metric breakdowns, compare them with Graphite, Sturdy, Semimak
and Canary, and state how far from optimal they can be shown to be.

\end{paperabstract}
\begin{paperbody}
\section{Research questions}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setlength{\itemsep}{1pt}\setlength{\parskip}{0pt}
\item
  RQ1 Which optimizer reaches the best layout fastest, by budget
  (anytime curves, performance profiles, time-to-target over 30 seeds)?
\item
  RQ2 How large is the provable gap; how does it shrink with fewer free
  keys?
\item
  RQ3 Are heuristic optima window-optimal (every k-key subset, k =
  6..12, solved exactly)?
\item
  RQ4 What is the best layout per board/corpus/profile, and how does it
  differ from the references on each metric?
\item
  RQ5 Does the answer change with symbols, layers and magic keys (code
  corpus, 36-key board)?
\end{enumerate}

\section{Hypotheses}

H1 BLS and SA tie at long budgets, BLS leads at short ones (matches the
2 s leaderboard). H2 $\geq$ 95 \% of windows with k $\leq$ 10 are exactly optimal
for the best heuristics. H3 misses are trigram-dominated. H4 the global
best equals the multi-seed consensus best. All can fail.

\section{Method}

\begin{itemize}
\setlength{\itemsep}{1pt}\setlength{\parskip}{0pt}
\item
  Algorithms under the \texttt{Optimizer} trait;
  \texttt{gecko\ bench\ -\/-seeds\ 30} over a budget grid.
\item
  Bound: QAP form (\texttt{Scorer::qap\_terms}), trigrams relaxed to
  pairs, GL plus 20 dual-ascent iterations; pins as constants.
\item
  Exact: branch and bound with the bound; MIP/CP-SAT oracle (\#43) for
  larger windows.
\item
  Reproducibility: every cited layout comes from a run verified with
  \texttt{gecko\ verify}.
\end{itemize}

\section{Existing evidence}

2 s leaderboard (10 seeds): BLS 17.616 $\pm$ 0.081, SA 17.787 $\pm$ 0.145,
memetic 18.027 $\pm$ 0.352, tabu 18.960 $\pm$ 0.256
(\texttt{bench/memetic-2026-10-21/}); SA 20 s optimum 15.704 under the
current profile with seeds agreeing; bound table and ascent convergence
4.49 $\to$ 5.81 (\texttt{context/algorithms/bounds.md}); neighbourhood study
(\texttt{context/algorithms/README.md}).

\section{Figures}

F1 anytime curves with CIs · F2 performance profile · F3 gap vs free
keys · F4 window-optimality share by algorithm and k · F5 best layout
keyboard + per-metric waterfall vs Graphite · F6 best layouts across
boards and corpora.

\section{Threats}

“Best” is relative to the cost function (see paper 2); weak bound at
full size; machine-dependent timings; one language unless the
multilingual runs are added.

\section{Needed}

\#43 oracle; window driver; 30-seed budget grid; final runs saved as
curated \texttt{bench/} directories.

\end{paperbody}
